title: BSA — Declaration of Purpose
text: It is the purpose of the Bank Secrecy Act to require certain reports or records that are highly useful in criminal, tax, or regulatory investigations or proceedings, or in the conduct of intelligence or counterintelligence activities to protect against international terrorism.

title: Customer Identification Program — Minimum Requirements
text: A bank's Customer Identification Program must include risk-based procedures for verifying the identity of each customer to the extent reasonable and practicable. At a minimum the bank must obtain the customer's name, date of birth for an individual, address, and identification number before opening an account.

title: CIP — Verification Through Documents
text: The CIP must contain procedures describing when the bank will rely on documents, non-documentary methods, or a combination of both to verify customer identity. Documentary verification for an individual may use an unexpired government-issued identification evidencing nationality or residence and bearing a photograph.

title: Beneficial Ownership Requirements for Legal Entity Customers
text: Covered financial institutions must establish and maintain written procedures to identify and verify the beneficial owners of legal entity customers at account opening, including each individual who owns 25 percent or more of the equity interests and a single individual with significant managerial control.

title: Anti-Money-Laundering Program Requirements
text: Each bank must develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program reasonably designed to prevent the bank from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing of terrorist activities. The program must include internal controls, independent testing, a designated BSA compliance officer, and ongoing training.

title: Customer Due Diligence — Ongoing Monitoring
text: Customer due diligence procedures must include understanding the nature and purpose of customer relationships to develop a customer risk profile, and conducting ongoing monitoring to identify and report suspicious transactions and, on a risk basis, to maintain and update customer information.

title: Reports of Suspicious Transactions (SAR)
text: A bank shall file a Suspicious Activity Report for any transaction conducted or attempted by, at, or through the bank involving or aggregating at least $5,000 in funds where the bank knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect the transaction involves funds derived from illegal activity, is designed to evade BSA requirements, or has no apparent lawful purpose.

title: Currency Transaction Report Filing Obligation
text: Each financial institution shall file a Currency Transaction Report for each deposit, withdrawal, exchange of currency, or other payment or transfer, by, through, or to the institution which involves a transaction in currency of more than $10,000.

title: Aggregation of Currency Transactions
text: Multiple currency transactions shall be treated as a single transaction if the financial institution has knowledge that they are by or on behalf of any person and result in either cash in or cash out totaling more than $10,000 during any one business day.

title: Enhanced Due Diligence for Correspondent Accounts
text: A covered financial institution shall apply enhanced due diligence to correspondent accounts established or maintained for foreign banks, including reasonable steps to identify foreign-bank ownership and to assess the money laundering risk presented by the correspondent account.

title: Prohibition on Correspondent Accounts for Shell Banks
text: A covered financial institution shall not establish, maintain, administer, or manage a correspondent account in the United States for, or on behalf of, a foreign shell bank that has no physical presence in any country.

title: Information Sharing Between Government and Institutions (314(a))
text: Upon receiving an information request from FinCEN, a financial institution shall expeditiously search its records to determine whether it maintains or has maintained any account for, or has engaged in any transaction with, each individual, entity, or organization named in the request.

title: Blocking and Reporting of Sanctioned Persons
text: Any U.S. person holding property in which a designated or blocked person has an interest must block the property and report the blocking to the Office of Foreign Assets Control. Engaging in transactions with sanctioned persons is prohibited absent a license.

title: FATF Recommendation 10 — Customer Due Diligence
text: Financial institutions should be required to undertake customer due diligence measures when establishing business relations, carrying out occasional transactions above the applicable threshold, where there is a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, or where there are doubts about the veracity of previously obtained identification data.
